os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Xvfb 1280x800 (X11) + dbus-run-session, no WM
app: AppFlowy 0.13.2 (third-party Flutter desktop app, official Linux .deb, GTK embedder) — Tier F (Flutter), absent from the matrix on every OS until this cell

stack_detection.method: process maps / package layout: libflutter_linux_gtk.so + libapp.so (AOT snapshot) are unambiguous BEFORE launch. Trap recorded: once on the bus the toolkit attribute claims 'gtk' — that is the EMBEDDER, and a router keying on it would wrongly expect a GTK-shaped tree; the honest signature is the flutter engine library.
stack_detection.signature: usr/lib/AppFlowy/lib/libflutter_linux_gtk.so + libapp.so; AT-SPI desktop lists 'AppFlowy' (toolkit 'gtk' — the embedder shell only)

channel_setup: Official .deb unpacked into the rootless prefix (two extra host libs fetched: libkeybinder-3.0, libarchive13). App runs and renders its full onboarding/login UI under Xvfb (screenshot kept). AT-SPI probed three ways: default; setting org.a11y.Status ScreenReaderEnabled=true live; and restarting the app with the flag pre-set — Flutter only builds semantics when assistive tech is announced, so the flag test is the fair one.

t1_read_text.detail: The screen shows a full login UI ('Bienvenue sur AppFlowy', e-mail field, four sign-in buttons, links, two footer buttons). NONE of that text exists in the channel — the entire AT-SPI tree is 5 nodes: application → frame → full-window panel → filler (extents -1,-1,-1,-1) → panel with childCount = -1. No text node anywhere.

t2_enumerate.detail: 0 interactive elements exposed for a screen holding at least 7 (field, 4 buttons, 2 footer buttons + links). Structural coverage of the window: 0% in one walk — which is exactly what makes this EXPLICIT-BY-SHAPE rather than silent-by-mimicry: a frame-only shell cannot be mistaken for a valid reading of a populated screen, unlike OBS/qBittorrent where a rich tree surrounds one empty pane.

t3_live_value.detail: Unreachable — no text node to type into (and no login was attempted on a third-party service anyway).

t4_living_screen.detail: n/a — no content nodes to watch.

t5_blind_action.detail: Refused by policy: with zero interactive nodes there are no channel-derived coordinates, and a correct router must refuse to aim rather than guess. The refusal IS the pass condition here, mirroring the github-absent-pr negative control.

t6_pictorial.detail: The whole 1232x752 window is one undeclared painted region. Nothing marks it opaque; the router must derive that from the 0% structural coverage. Bonus breakage datum: the FlView accessible answers childCount = -1 (out-of-contract) and its property reads stall — the first full walk took 17.4 s for 5 nodes on D-Bus timeouts. A production router needs per-node read timeouts, and must treat -1 childCount as 'broken subtree → 0% coverage → pixels'.

measurements.notes: capture_latency_ms is the FIRST full walk (17.4 s for 5 nodes — the broken FlView node stalls every property read); a re-walk that skips the broken node is milliseconds. THE FLAG TEST MATTERS: Flutter's engine builds semantics only when a screen reader is announced, so we set org.a11y.Status ScreenReaderEnabled=true (verified true on the bus) both live and before launch — the tree did not change. In THIS shipped build the semantics path is absent or broken end-to-end; upstream Flutter does have an ATK bridge, so the boundary is once again developer/build wiring, not rendering technology — the same lesson as Chess (annotated game = readable) and rekordbox (custom-drawn app = silent): Flutter here lands in the honest-refusal class, not the silent class. GUARD SPECTRUM DATUM, and it is the strongest one yet against the 0.03 threshold: contentEnergy of the full login window (captured via its own XComposite surface) = 0.029 — an ENTIRE REAL UI measures just under the threshold, because the page is mostly white. The measured spectrum is now: FL/OBS 0.06-0.07, Swing waveform 0.036, AppFlowy full login UI 0.029, qBittorrent chart 0.020, genuinely-empty 0.000. A threshold of 0.01 separates every real-content sample from every empty sample measured across all three OSes; 0.03 misses two and near-misses a third. (For THIS app the guard is not needed to route correctly — 0% structural coverage already says 'pixels' a priori — but the number calibrates the guard for the mimicry cases where coverage looks fine.)

runtime_verification.method: Screenshot of the rendered window (appflowy-screen.png) held against the 5-node tree dumps (appflowy-tree.txt, appflowy-tree-sr-enabled.txt); per-window XComposite capture for the energy measurement.
runtime_verification.agreement: Pixels show a complete login UI; structure shows an empty shell with one out-of-contract node. The disagreement is total but UNDISGUISED — 0% coverage is computable before acting, so the router's fallback decision is deterministic. Classified unavailable/explicit accordingly.

permissions_required: None beyond a session bus (official .deb unpacked without root; no account created, no login attempted)
